targetPopulation: Public https finance and news sites drawn from an externally defined universe (a permanent-id source snapshot named in the candidate-universe manifest), each having served two bare-load-valid visits during the preregistered reliability sweep. Rates describe THIS population only and are not an estimate for the web. No base rate is assumed: the CNAME prevalence of this population is unknown until independently justified from scope data, and sizing is re-derived under the step-3 policy-C decision from the sweep's cluster-aware loss bound before any frame seals. The detector's 10-host lookup cap is an instrument property disclosed to readers, never a population boundary: a visit that exceeds it is conserved as a measurement-lossy case under policy C, not excluded.

design.selectionProtocol: Frame drawn by seeded simple random sampling from the externally defined candidate universe (source order, exclusion-only repository input, per the candidate-universe provenance artifact), every candidate having passed the reliability sweep's eligibility pair under the exact measurement condition. The pre-qualification probe is a bare load check that never evaluates the detector or records its output; a full scan before the frame is sealed would mean predictions were seen before preregistration. No candidate is excluded for exceeding the detector's 10-host lookup cap: that is selection on measurement difficulty, and policy C conserves such cases in the envelope instead. Frame size N is NOT fixed by this draft: it is derived before sealing from the sweep's cluster-aware loss bound together with an independently justified prevalence estimate for the declared scope, and the derivation is recorded in the preregistration. The random seed is the SHA-256 of this study's committed preregistration.json, recorded in the frame tooling output.
design.referenceProtocol: Each labeler independently establishes ground truth WITHOUT any input produced by this scanner. Using their own browser capture of the case URL, they enumerate the hostnames under the site's registrable domain that the page caused their browser to contact, skipping only the registrable apex so the candidate boundary matches the detector's (lib/cname-uncloaking.ts cnameCloakCandidates). They resolve each candidate's CNAME chain through a resolver they name, and assert present when a chain reaches a host matched by an external, publicly published tracking-service list they pin by SHA-256; absent otherwise. A case in which any candidate could not be resolved is not determined and must not be labelled absent. The recorded DNS chains produced by this project's scanner and this project's tracker catalog are NOT admissible reference inputs: a labeler reading them would reproduce our resolver's and our catalog's errors exactly, and the study would report that agreement as accuracy. npm run calibration:cname-reference builds the worksheet; the labeler forms their own judgement and seals their own source.
design.adjudicationProtocol: Two through ten distinct GitHub actors label every case independently and blind to each other. One additional distinct actor precommits a blind tiebreaker source before acquisition. Agreements stand as final. Any disagreement is resolved by the precommitted tiebreaker alone, recorded as disagreement-resolved-by-blind-tiebreaker with the tiebreaker identity and artifact digest; no post-hoc discussion, relabeling, or majority vote occurs.

measurementCondition.interpretation: Rates are conditional on desktop visits with GPC disabled under passive consent observation with no consent action.
